device.name: Chef iQ Sense
device.notes: Smart thermometer hub (CQ60) with wireless probes and ESP32-WROVER-E chipset. DUAL-INTERFACE: it works LOCALLY over BLE (probe data + Wi-Fi provisioning) AND has a network component for REMOTE work — once provisioned it joins the LAN (Wi-Fi; the mains-powered base can also sit on wired Ethernet) and connects OUTBOUND to Chef iQ's cloud (AWS IoT MQTT) for remote monitoring. DISCOVERY: because that network side is an outbound cloud connection, the hub advertises NO local service (no mDNS/SSDP/Bonjour observed), so a passive LAN scan cannot find it — it is discovered over BLE (manufacturer ID 0x05CD, name "CQ60"). If a network capture ever shows a local advertisement, add a Wi-Fi discovery method then; the captures on hand are BLE (Bluetooth H4) only. Uses BLE for probe communication and Wi-Fi provisioning; Wi-Fi for cloud (AWS IoT MQTT). React Native app whose protocol logic lives in a Hermes bytecode bundle, recovered by static analysis. Five BLE UUID families for different device generations and functions. BLE manufacturer ID: 0x05CD. Device name: exactly "CQ60". Temperatures are IEEE 754 single-precision floats; the unit on the wire is NOT determinable from the app code (parseBytesData is a plain readFloatLE with no conversion) and is governed by the writable 9C6FFFC0 Temperature Unit characteristic. Probe data uses TLV (Tag-Length-Value) binary encoding with typed attribute IDs. Three command channels: thermometer (048A), system (9C6F), FTP/OTA (F640). Cloud: api.chefiq.com (REST), graph.chefiq.com (GraphQL), iot.chefiq.com (MQTT). The same endpoints also appear verbatim in the app's string resources, which additionally name media.chefiq.com, {service}-api.chefiq.com/v1, and the link.chefiq.com deep-link domain. Firmware-update metadata comes from the REST API: GET /check-for-updates with an x-api-key header (key embedded in the app; value not reproduced here) and query params model_number, manifest_version, generation, hw_version, esp_version, msp_version. The binary itself is delivered to the hub as an ota_server_url pushed over the MQTT 'ota' config key, then transferred device-side; the BLE F640 FTP service is the alternative app-driven transfer path. Auth: AWS Cognito. The identity-pool id us-east-1:f95270e2-a024-41dc-bf5e-2d5df159f259 is a PUBLIC client-side identifier (region:uuid format), NOT a secret credential -- it ships in every copy of the app (present both in the Hermes bundle and in the app's string resources as COGNITO_IDENTITY_POOL_ID) and grants nothing without a valid user login. Retained here (and in docs/devices/chef-iq-sense.md) for interoperability; no vendor secret is published. No certificate pinning. MQTT topics: ciq-v2/dt/thermometer/{cognito_id}~{device_id}/+ (the app's subscribe list also includes ciq-v2/cmd/app/.../res/+, ciq-v2/evt/thermometer/.../ota-response and .../notification/+ plus the $aws/events/presence topics). Wi-Fi provisioning over BLE via Family C (8A71) characteristics, versioned V1/V2/V3. ADVERTISEMENT PATH (connectionless, no GATT needed): probes broadcast temperatures and battery unauthenticated in manufacturer data 0x05CD -- a simpler local integration than the GATT protocol below. Packet type is the low nibble of byte 0 (0x0 ASCII name, 0x1 temperature, 0x3 status with MAC + battery on newer versions); the remaining nibbles carry a major.minor.patch protocol version decoded as major = byte 1 high nibble, minor = byte 1 low nibble, patch = byte 0 high nibble (5.0.0 seen on current CQ60). Probe payloads are at most 18 bytes; the hub advertises under the same manufacturer ID with a longer (>= 20 B) payload -- a clean programmatic discriminator from probes. Temperature packet (type 0x1), V3 layout (protocol major >= 3; hardware-verified against a live CQ60 at 5.0.0 by chefiq_ble): ambient [2:4], food [4:6], tip1 [6:8], tip2 [8:10], tip3 [10:12], tip4 [12:14], ambient mirror [14:16]. All temperatures are signed int16 little-endian in tenths of a degree C; an unmeasured ring sends a sentinel >= 0x7FF0 (0x7FFB typical), and consumers should drop any decoded temperature outside the plausible window -40..600 C rather than surface a sentinel. Status packet (type 0x3, V3, min 10 bytes): battery percent byte at [8], SoC temperature (raw byte, whole degrees C) at [9], probe MAC in the same packet. Older layouts (reconstructed, NOT hardware-verified): V2 (major == 2) carries battery [2], soc [3], ambient [4:6], food [6:8], tip1-3 [8:10]..[12:14], ambient mirror [14:16]; legacy carries MAC [2:8], battery [8], soc [9], food [10:12], ambient [12:14], ambient mirror [14:16]. Battery scaling is CONTESTED between the cited sources: ITSpecialist111 documents the battery byte as 0-255 mapping to 0-100 %, while chefiq_ble (the hardware-verified implementation) emits the raw byte directly as the percent with no scaling -- treat the exact scaling as unconfirmed until checked against a probe at a known charge. Sources: Invader444/chefiq-ble (PyPI), ble_monitor >= 12.8.0 (added CQ60 passive decoding), ITSpecialist111 ChefIQ integration, formula97/homeassistant-chefiq. FCC IDs: hub 2AC7Z-ESP32WROVERE (modular approval, ESP32-WROVER-E); probes 2A2YP-CQ60QPROBE (earlier v1 grant 2A2YP-CQ60PROBE; ISED IC 27740-CQ60QPROBE; a 2024-12-18 FCC C2PC adds probe models CQ60-PRC-01/02/03/04).

credentials.notes: BLE writes here are not encrypted or bonded, so the passphrase is exposed to anything sniffing the connection event during provisioning. Provision in a quiet RF environment or skip WiFi entirely for local use.
stored_on_device: AWS IoT device identity for cloud MQTT

factory_reset.effect: Removing the stored credential over BLE unprovisions WiFi without touching probe pairings or the account.

steps.notes: Protocol-level unprovision; the hardware button sequence for a full reset is not documented here.

methods.description: For local use, no provisioning is required: scan for the local name CQ60, connect, and use the thermometer (048A) and system (9C6F) services directly.
methods.name: BLE only — no provisioning at all

steps.action: Scan for a device advertising the local name CQ60 with manufacturer ID 0x05CD and connect.

methods.description: WiFi credentials are written over the Family C service. The characteristic set is versioned V1/V2/V3 across device generations, so read the network-info characteristic first and match the version before writing.
methods.name: Wi-Fi credentials over the provisioning service

steps.action: Read the network info characteristic to learn the provisioning version and current state.
Read the scanned-network characteristic to enumerate visible access points.
Write the target SSID and passphrase to the set-network characteristic.
steps.notes: Payload is a UTF-8 JSON object ({"connect": {...}} to join, {"forget": "<ssid>"} to forget) — see the Set Wi-Fi Network characteristic notes.

steps.action: Subscribe to the network info characteristic for the join result.

setup.notes: The CQ60 hub is a BLE device that also needs WiFi, and the two roles are cleanly separated: probes and live readings work over BLE with no setup at all, while cloud/MQTT features need the WiFi credentials that are pushed over the Family C (8A71) provisioning service. A local-first client can stop after BLE and never provision WiFi — worth saying out loud, because the vendor app treats the account as mandatory.

rejoin.notes: BLE stays available whatever the WiFi state, so a new network is just another write to 8a71ffa3 — optionally preceded by a remove-credential write to 8a71ffa5. No physical reset needed.

entities.name: Internal Temperature
entities.notes: Consumes TLV attribute 36 (InternalTemp, float32) from the Probe Data notify — attribute ID and type confirmed in the vendor app; see that characteristic's notes for the TLV frame layout (no fixed offsets — parse the envelope). Unit source is a device setting, not fixed: the wire float32 carries no unit (the app applies no conversion in the decode path), so read the active unit from the 9C6FFFC0 Temperature Unit characteristic's temp_unit field (unit_reference 9c6fffc0-…-dc5a.temp_unit; unit_values 0 = °F, 1 = °C) before rendering. No out-of-box default unit is claimed here because none is evidenced — the app writes the setting from the phone locale on setup. Consumers that want an unambiguous reading can instead use the connectionless advertisement path (int16 LE, 0.1 °C), which is always in °C.

entities.name: Ambient Temperature
entities.notes: Consumes TLV attribute 37 (AmbientTemp, float32) from the Probe Data notify — same decode path and caveats as Internal Temperature. Unit source is a device setting: read the active unit from the 9C6FFFC0 temp_unit field (unit_reference 9c6fffc0-…-dc5a.temp_unit; unit_values 0 = °F, 1 = °C) before rendering; no out-of-box default is claimed (none evidenced). The connectionless advertisement path (int16 LE, 0.1 °C) remains the unambiguous °C alternative.

characteristics.name: Probe Data
characteristics.notes: Notifications carry TLV (Tag-Length-Value) records with typed attribute IDs; temperatures are IEEE 754 float32 (SingleFloat). The app applies NO unit conversion in the decode path (parseBytesData is a plain readFloatLE), so the unit on the wire is NOT determinable from the code; it is governed by the writable 9C6FFFC0 Temperature Unit characteristic. TLV frame layout, read directly from the app's own parser (processBLEData / parseBytesData in its Hermes bundle): a sequence of attribute entries, each [attr_id uint16 LE][type uint8][length uint8][value length bytes]. The per-entry type byte (DataTypeEnum: 0 bool, 1-6 signed/unsigned 8/16/32-bit LE ints, 7 SignedInt64, 8 UnsignedInt64, 9 float32 LE rounded to 2 decimals, 10 DoubleFloat, 11 utf8 string, 12 hex byte array, 13 MAC address, 14 JSON) drives decoding. One notification can carry several per-probe records: a new record starts when an attribute ID repeats, and attribute 16 (probe_address, MAC) is the record delimiter. Attribute IDs (AttributeEnum, confirmed in the same bundle): 0 Timestamp (u32), 16 ProbeAddress (MAC), 17 Type (i8), 19 HwVersion (str), 20 FwVersion (str), 21 SerialNumber (str), 22 ServiceConfig (u8), 23 Name (str), 24 Registered (bool), 25 DockNumber (u8 -- which hub dock slot the probe sits in), 26 Size, 27 Color, 28 Number, 29 IsIncompatible (bool), 32 IsActive (bool -- probe docked/charging state), 33 Rssi (i8), 34 BatteryLevel (uint8), 35 IcTemp (f32), 36 InternalTemp (f32), 37 AmbientTemp (f32), 38 IsOverheat (bool), 39 IsSensorFail (bool), 40-43 Tip1-Tip4 temps (f32), 44 Ext1Temp (f32). The same enum defines session attributes 48-90 and notification attributes 91-123 -- see 048af001 Session Data. Because records are tagged, fields have NO fixed byte offsets, so no declarative format block is possible — parse the TLV envelope instead. Confidence: confirmed against the app's parser code, not yet against hardware. Neither downloaded RE implementation (Invader444/chefiq-ble, ble_monitor) decodes this GATT characteristic; both document only the connectionless advertisement path (manufacturer data 0x05CD, signed int16 LE in 0.1 °C, sentinel >= 0x7FF0, per-probe slots), which does NOT mirror this notify's encoding (int16 0.1 °C vs float32). Consumers who just need probe temperatures can also use the documented advertisement path in the device notes above.

characteristics.name: Session Data
characteristics.notes: TLV-encoded like 048af000 Probe Data (same frame layout and per-entry DataTypeEnum); records are split on attribute 48 (SessionId) as the delimiter. Session attribute IDs from the app's attribute enum: 48 SessionId (str), 49 CookingCategory (u8), 50 CookingMethod (u8), 51 PresetId (str), 56 CookingTime (u32), 57 EstimatedCookingTime (u32), 59 TargetTemp (f32), 60 RecipeId (str), 61 GuidedId (str), 62 AutoCancel (bool), 80 RemainingTime (u32), 81 TotalElapsedTime (u32), 82 ProgressPercent (f32), 83 FlipStatus (bool), 84 OperatingState (u8), 85 OperatingWarning (u8), 86 OperatingError (u8), 88 RemainingCookingTime (u32), 89 SessionInternalTemp (f32), 90 SessionAmbientTemp (f32). The same enum also defines session metadata attributes the earlier listing skipped: 52 SessionName (str), 53 SessionIcon (str), 54 SessionImage (str), 55 SessionDescription (str), 58 SessionIdleTimeout, 63 NotificationKey, 87 CookingStateNotificationId, 91 IsReminder, 92 CookingStateIsRunning. The enum further defines notification attributes 93-123 (93 NotificationConditionStatus, 94 NotificationConditionMetCount, 112 NotificationId, 113 NotificationCategory, 114 NotificationDescription, 115 NotificationStepIndex, 116 NotificationReminder, 117 NotificationTriggerStart, 118 NotificationTimer, 119 NotificationAudioClips, 120 NotificationCondition, 121 NotificationEstimatedTime, 122 NotificationTriggerCancel, 123 IgnoreOnStart) -- these ride in TLV records returned by the cooking-state/session notification commands, distinct from the plain-JSON payloads of 048af020/21/22. Confidence: confirmed against the app's parser code, not yet against hardware.

register_probe.description: Register a probe to the hub

characteristics.name: Thermometer Command Response
characteristics.notes: Responses carry an 8-byte header: commandId u8 @0, requestId u32 LE @1, responseCode int8 @5, size u16 LE @6, followed by `size` payload bytes. Attribute-bearing commands (e.g. get_probe_attributes, start_session) return payloads in the same TLV encoding as 048af000 Probe Data. responseCode values (CommandAPIResponse enum in the app's shared constants module, consumed by the command error-mapping path): 0 OK, -1 FAIL, -2 ERR_INVALID_COMMAND, -3 ERR_HEAP_ALLOC, -4 ERR_MOUNT_POINT, -5 ERR_PARTITION, -6 ERR_DIGEST, -7 ERR_SIZE, -8 ERR_WRITE; the enum sits beside the FTP command constants and appears shared across the command services. Evidence: the app's header-processing path and its CommandAPIResponse enum. Confidence: app-derived, not hardware-verified.

characteristics.name: Battery Status
characteristics.notes: Charge state enum: 0 = discharging, 1 = charging (BatteryStatus enum in the app; an absent value defaults to discharging). Evidence: the app's Hermes bundle.

characteristics.name: Battery Level
characteristics.notes: Signed int16 little-endian, no scaling; the app consumes the raw value directly as the battery level (0-100 % by usage — no explicit range check in code). The app's characteristic registry declares read+notify and subscribes to it (the earlier read-only listing was wrong). Evidence: the app's Hermes bundle.

characteristics.name: Signature
characteristics.notes: Registry data type String (UTF-8). Evidence: the app's characteristic registry.

characteristics.name: Data Update Interval
characteristics.notes: Registry key dt_update_interval, data type UnsignedInt32 (uint32 LE) — the probe-data telemetry cadence. Evidence: the app's characteristic registry.

characteristics.name: System Command Request
characteristics.notes: Command IDs confirmed against the app's system-command enum. Quirk: the enum spells command 1 "FactoryVersion", but the CQ60 registry maps that same enum member to the key 'factory-reset' — command 1 is the factory-reset command; the enum name is a vendor typo.

characteristics.name: Set Wi-Fi Network
characteristics.notes: Payload is a UTF-8 JSON object. To join a network the app writes {"connect": <network>} where <network> is the selected scan entry (fields ssid/auth/rssi, extended with the entered passphrase); to forget one it writes {"forget": "<ssid>"}. Evidence: the app's connectToWifi and forgetNetwork sagas; the exact passphrase field name inside the connect object is not pinned down there.

services.name: Wi-Fi Provisioning Service (Family C)
services.notes: Every characteristic in this service is registered with data type String (UTF-8) in the CQ60 profile of the app's characteristic registry. Payloads are JSON: the app serializes writes with JSON.stringify. Scanned-network entries carry {ssid, auth, rssi} fields.
